sources.entry: scikit-surprise - A scikit for building and analyzing recommender systems.

summary.one_liner: Surprise is a Python scikit for building, evaluating, and comparing recommender systems that work on explicit rating data.
summary.what_it_does: Provides ready-to-use rating-prediction algorithms, including baselines, neighborhood methods (k-NN variants), matrix factorization (SVD, PMF, SVD++, NMF), Slope One, and Co-Clustering. It includes built-in similarity measures such as cosine, MSD, and Pearson. It loads built-in datasets (MovieLens, Jester) or custom datasets. It offers cross-validation iterators modeled on scikit-learn and exhaustive parameter search (GridSearchCV). The README includes benchmark RMSE/MAE/time tables on MovieLens 100k and 1M. It does not support implicit ratings or content-based information.
use_cases: compare recommender algorithms on rating data
evaluate rating prediction accuracy with RMSE and MAE
tune algorithm parameters with grid search
build a recommender from custom explicit ratings
how_to_run: git clone the repo, cd surprise, pip install . (requires Cython and numpy)
notable: Built-in MovieLens and Jester dataset loading with automatic download
Classic collaborative filtering and matrix factorization algorithms in one API
Cross-validation and exhaustive parameter search modeled on scikit-learn
Published benchmark tables for default parameters on MovieLens 100k and 1M
caveats: Only maintained since version 1.1.0 (September 2019): bugfixes and occasional performance work, no new features
Does not support implicit ratings or content-based information
Building from source requires Cython and numpy
